title: What a p-value is
summary: A tail probability under the null, not a posterior and not an effect size.

choices.text: If the null hypothesis were true, a result at least this extreme would occur about 3% of the time.
Given the data, there is a 3% probability that the null hypothesis is true, so the alternative is 97% likely.
If the experiment were repeated, there is a 97% chance it would again be significant at the 0.05 level.
The effect is large enough to matter in practice, since a p-value this small rules out a trivial difference.
